* * *
 JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed the claim petition U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 28.02.2024 at about 12.30 p.m, the petitioner was proceeding as passenger in the Auto rickshaw came from Kallahalli Village to Bengaluru, (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 while he reached Malekoppalu Flyover, near Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan District, at that time Lorry bearing No.TN-29-BU-3015 parked without any sign board and precautions in road side.
Due to this wrong parking of the lorry, Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AL-5863 was dashed to the offending lorry.
Due to which the petitioner was sitting as passenger suffered lot as well as auto was damaged and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
he was taken first aid treatment at Government hospital, Channarayapatna and Hassan and later he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru and Minto hospital,
wherein he was treated as inpatient from 29.02.2024 to 17.03.2024 and from 29.03.2024 to 02.04.2024 respectively and he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization, transportation, medicines and nourishment and prior to the accident,
the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 59 years and was working as Auto Driver and doing Real estate business and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. On account of the accidental injuries, he is not able to continue his work and he is under complete bed-rest, as such incurring loss of income from the date of accident till date and suffering (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 from permanent disability and undergo severe mental stress and agony.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry and in this regard the Channarayapatna Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the offending lorry.

The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioner together with cost and interest.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry, alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending lorry, age, avocation and income of petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by the Shankar R vs Palani M on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62422073/
2 petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not in possession of valid driving licence to drive the said class of vehicle and there is no (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 valid permit, fitness certificate to the offending lorry, hence, there is violation of policy conditions by the owner and the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

The compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 28.02.2024 at about 12.30 p.m, near Malekoppalu flyover, NH-75 Channarayapatna Taluk, Hasana District, due to negligent parking of Lorry bearing registration No. TN-29-BU-3015 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove his case, the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and got examined Doctors as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16 and closed his side evidence.

By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 counsel submits no oral evidence and hence, the respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.
08.
Heard both sides.

09. My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1
Partly
in the Affirmative Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3

As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

In his cross-examination he stated that he was working as auto driver, now he is not working and he was the owner of Auto bearing No.KA-03-AL-5863 and one Abhishek was driving the auto and admits that he and his wife were going as a passenger and the accident road is two way and having divider Shankar R vs Palani M on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62422073/
3 in the center of the road and admits that usually the lorries was parking on the side of the road (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 and denied to the suggestion that his auto driver was driving the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed against rear right side of the lorry and caused the accident and due to this the auto driver died on the spot and admits that in Charge sheet the auto driver Abhishek made as accused No.1.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Channarayapatna Traffic Police against driver of the offending Lorry.
Ex.P.2 is Complaint shows due to rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry the accident was occurred and due to which the petitioner sustained injuries.

Ex.P.3 is Charge sheet shows after completion of investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of Auto rickshaw as A1 and owner/driver of the Lorry as A2, for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.122, 177 of MV Act, for the reasons that the driver of Auto rickshaw drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against rear portion of the lorry which was parked without any precautionary measures and caused the accident.
Due to which the driver of Auto rickshaw died on the spot.

Ex.P.4 and 5 are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident on near the land of Devaraju Mallenahalli, (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 Malekoppalu flyover, NH-75 Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan District, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is IMV report which discloses involvement of both vehicles in the accident and more damages caused to the Auto rickshaw.
It is opined that the said accident was not due to any mechanical defects of motor vehicles.

Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate which shows that the petitioner sustained 1) Right ear bleed and B/L nasal bleed +, 2)
Multiple abrasion injuries + over face, 3) Lacerated injury + over occipital region measuring 1 x 0.5 x 3 cm, 4) B/L peri orbital oedema +, 5) Multiple abrasion injury + over left upper limb with swelling and deformity at forearm.
Closed mid shaft of ulna fracture left side and the doctor has opined that injury No.5 is grievous in nature and rest are simple in nature.
Ex.P.8 is the Discharge summary shows the petitioner sustained closed mid shaft of ulna fracture left side.
Ex.P.9 is Outpatient record.
On going through the above said documents, it is clear that the accident occurred due to some negligence on the part of the driver of Auto rickshaw.
Therefore, it is clear that there is a contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the Auto rickshaw also this accident occurred.

Hence, some (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 contributory negligence taken on the part of the petitioner's Auto rickshaw driver in the accident, but major negligence is taken on the part of the driver of the offending lorry.
Accordingly, apportion of the negligence on the part of the petitioner's Auto rickshaw driver is taken at 40% and 60% on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry.
To disprove the case of the petitioner, the respondent No.2 did not lead evidence.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 59 years and was working as Auto Driver and doing Real estate business and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
transportation, medicines and nourishment.
On account of the accidental injuries, he could not attend to his work and lost his earnings and has became permanent disabled.

sentences.text: It is the duty of the petitioner to prove his age, the petitioner has produced Aadhaar card and Driving licence as per Ex.P.11 and 12, which discloses his date of birth as 06.06.1965 and the alleged accident was occurred on 28.02.2024 and hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is 59 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, considering the said documents, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 59 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case, the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 years is '9'.
13.

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,500/-
and it is multiplied by 12.
14.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained fracture of mid shaft of ulna (L) and other injuries and radiological examination shows fracture united with implant in-situ and he assessed permanent physical disability of 24% of left upper limb, which is 8% to the whole body and he has produced Recent X-rays, OPD card and Inpatient case sheet as per Ex.P.13 to 15.
In his cross-examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and treated doctor is available in their hospital and he has not taken opinion of treated doctor.
At the time of discharge doctor advise not to lift heavy weights for a period of 3 months.

Fracture is united and denied to the suggestion that the restrictions mentioned in para 3 of his affidavit is not due to accidental injuries but due to his age old ailments and admits that in their hospital various schemes are available.
Under ABRK scheme he has given treatment.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Ophthalmologist at Srikara Eye Clinic, Bengaluru, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that during admission of petitioner at Victoria hospital was advised repair of comeo-scleral tear of right eye once the general condition of patient is stable.

Later he was admitted to Minto hospital and underwent comeo- scleral tear repair and petitioner's right eye is having phthisis bulbi and vision in right eye is totally and irreversibly lost and he assessed petitioner's visual disability to 30% and he has produced Original outpatient record as per Ex.P.16.
In his cross- examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally.
Corneo-scleral tear now it is cured.
Now eye ball is shrunk.
Even petitioner cannot perceive the light.
PL means perception of light.
Right eye totally blind, left eye being normal and admits that the petitioner might have sustained above injuries due to some other cause.
In Minto hospital eye specialist advised eye drops.
I have assessed the disability only for the vision not for the whole body.

However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and PW.3 and nature of Shankar R vs Palani M on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62422073/
5 injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 18%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.16,500/- x 12 x 9 x 18/100 = Rs.3,20,760/-.
16.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Discharge summary of Victoria hospital and Minto hospital, Bengaluru, according to which he took treatment as inpatient totally for 23 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under this head.

17. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 and PW.3 doctors and X-rays, Inpatient case sheet, Outpatient record and on account of accidental injuries,
petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to fractures suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.40,000/-
under this head.
(SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 18. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,500/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 23 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least three months.

Thus,
taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.49,500/-
(Rs.16,500 x 3) under this head.
19. Medical expenses:- The petitioner has not produced any Medical bills.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled any compensation under this head.
20. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
(SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.5799/2024 21. Future medical expenses:-
According to doctor PW.2, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implant, but he not stated the actual cost and has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

As discussed in the Issue No.1, this tribunal already held that due to contributory negligence of the petitioner's Auto rickshaw driver and driver of offending Lorry this accident occurred, hence the petitioner's Auto rickshaw driver negligence part is taken at 40% and the driver of offending vehicle negligence is taken at 60% respectively.

24. Regarding liability:- On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared and respondent No.2 has filed objections and contested the matter, but

On the date of accident policy was in force.

Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:-
In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:- -
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
